facts: Codex subscription run 87830305-fb5a-4a69-bb00-35eb7c3d5613 completed with isMock=false and read only AGENTS.md, STATE.md and PROJECT_DOCS_INDEX.md from the candidate project.
The provider emitted a useful JSON object containing all requested planning keys, but prefixed it with a prose sentence; the strict parser therefore recorded PARTIAL and traceability_pass=false.
The proposed increment preserves fixture-only, read-only, localhost-only behavior and explicitly excludes real data, public service, tunnel, GPT-Live and user acceptance.

The candidate's existing npm test passed 9/9 fixture smoke checks with real_data_accessed=false after one elevated local-loopback retry; ordinary sandbox execution was blocked by EPERM on 127.0.0.1:18787.
No candidate file was modified and no public service or real knowledge data was accessed.
inferences: The project is a suitable second real-input validation target because its state and privacy boundary are explicit and its smoke test is repeatable.
The immediate Product Builder engineering gap is output normalization/strict validation, not another candidate-project feature.
unknowns: Whether the proposed offline evidence report improves repeated user work has not been measured.
No real-user acceptance, cost comparison, DeepSeek run or Codex native resume was performed.
The provider's JSON content was not accepted as a formal artifact under the current exact-wire contract.

verdict.next_decision: Implement a small current-workspace output-normalization and strict validation contract, with a fixture transcript test; only then schedule one new real provider run if the budget and state allow.
